summary: Re-review of all 16 units. The round-1 major issue and the five requested fixes were each confirmed independently in Python: weld-heat-flow summary now correctly separates the fusion zone (melted) from the HAZ (not melted); Q(4.00)=31.7 ppm and Q(5.00)=0.29 ppm; hot-rolling example mu=0.3, R=250 mm gives 22.5 mm draft, exit 37.5 mm, 37.5 percent; cost-structure carries an illustrative note and per-part overhead (4.75 total); the wear-limited run now counts 9 parts (part 9 = 40.017, part 10 = 40.021). Every numeric key, worked example and table figure across all units was recomputed (forging, extrusion, drawing, Chvorinov and riser, cost and break-even, chip geometry and forces, Taylor and economic life, PM density and force, LPBF and DED rates, bending, blanking, draw ratio and force, Cp/Cpk/ppm, RSS stacks, heat input, cooling rate, carbon equivalent, restrained stress, thermal expansion) and all match the keys within tolerance. No tab or control characters, non-ASCII, escaped-unicode text, object placeholders or TODO text were found in any packet. No critical or major problems remain; the seven minor items are wording or consistency points, six of which carry over unchanged from round 1. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: Explanation says a larger diameter gives "a lower rev/min but a longer path per turn". The cutting path length is L/f regardless of diameter; the real cause is that for fixed V, N = 1000V/(pi D) falls as 1/D, so t = L/(fN) rises in proportion to D. (Carried over from round 1.)
issues.suggestedFix: Explain via t = L/(fN) with N proportional to 1/D at constant cutting speed, so t is proportional to D.

issues.problem: Explanation says a larger shear angle shortens the shear plane "so less metal is sheared per unit time". At fixed speed and feed the removal rate is unchanged; what falls is shear-plane area and shear strain. (Carried over from round 1.)
issues.suggestedFix: Say the shorter shear plane has less shear area and lower shear strain, so cutting force and specific energy fall.

issues.problem: "A lathe spindle motor draws 6.0 kW at the shaft ... cutting power at the tool is 80 percent of the motor power." Power drawn "at the shaft" and "motor power" are mixed, so it is unclear whether 6.0 kW is input or output. (Carried over from round 1; key 4.0 J/mm^3 is correct.)
issues.suggestedFix: Say the machine draws 6.0 kW of input power and 80 percent of it reaches the cutting zone.

issues.problem: Compaction-force worked example gives "outside diameter of 60 mm" and "a pressing area of 1500 mm^2"; a full 60 mm disc is about 2827 mm^2, so the diameter is unused and confusing. (Carried over from round 1.)
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the diameter or state that a central hole or relief gives a net pressed area of 1500 mm^2.

issues.problem: Worked example says "Since 1.91 is below 2.0, a single draw is feasible" and the answer "one draw should work", but the lesson gives LDR as 1.8 to 2.0, so 1.91 lies inside the uncertain range. (Carried over from round 1.)
issues.suggestedFix: Say a single draw is marginal-to-feasible and must be checked against the sheet's measured LDR.

issues.problem: Marking guide asks for "a few micrometres (a tolerance grade around IT5 or IT6)" for a 45 mm seat; IT5 is about 11 micrometres and IT6 about 16 micrometres at that size. (Carried over from round 1.)
issues.suggestedFix: Say "about 10 to 16 micrometres (IT5 to IT6)" or drop the grade reference.

issues.problem: In the Cpk-to-ppm table the header says z = 3 Cpk, but rows are inconsistent: Cpk 0.67 shows z = 2.01 (3 x rounded 0.67, giving 22216 ppm) whereas 1.33 and 1.67 show z = 4.00 and 5.00 (exact 4/3 and 5/3). A student checking 3 x 1.33 = 3.99 will not match 4.00.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a note that Cpk values 1.33 and 1.67 are rounded from 4/3 and 5/3, and use z = 2.00 (2.275 percent, 22750 ppm) for 2/3 or label the 0.67 row as using the rounded value.
